.TH "SYMVAULT" "1" "Nov 2026" "Symaira Vault" "Symaira Vault Manual"

.SH NAME
symvault-add - Add a new password entry


.SH SYNOPSIS
\fBsymvault add  [flags]\fP


.SH DESCRIPTION
Creates a new password entry in the vault.

.PP
The entry name can use slash notation for organization (e.g., work/aws).
Interactive mode prompts for username, password, and URL.


.SH OPTIONS
\fB--allow-empty\fP[=false]
	Allow empty value for sensitive fields

.PP
\fB--auto-rotate\fP[=false]
	Enable automatic rotation reminder

.PP
\fB--expires-at\fP=""
	Expiration date (RFC3339 format)

.PP
\fB--force\fP[=false]
	Skip password strength validation

.PP
\fB--generate\fP[=false]
	Generate a secure password (non-interactive)

.PP
\fB-h\fP, \fB--help\fP[=false]
	help for add

.PP
\fB--length\fP=20
	Generated password length for --generate

.PP
\fB--notes\fP=""
	Notes (non-interactive)

.PP
\fB--stdin-totp-secret\fP[=false]
	Read TOTP secret from stdin (prevents argv leak)

.PP
\fB--stdin-value\fP[=false]
	Read password value from stdin (prevents argv leak)

.PP
\fB--totp-account\fP=""
	TOTP account name/username

.PP
\fB--totp-issuer\fP=""
	TOTP issuer/service name

.PP
\fB--totp-secret\fP=""
	TOTP secret key (base32 encoded, visible in process listings)

.PP
\fB--type\fP=""
	Secret type (api_key, bearer_token, basic_auth, ssh_key, password, certificate, database_url, totp_seed, custom). Auto-detected if not specified.

.PP
\fB--url\fP=""
	URL (non-interactive)

.PP
\fB--usage-hint\fP=""
	Usage hint for AI agents

.PP
\fB--username\fP=""
	Username (non-interactive)

.PP
\fB--value\fP=""
	Password value (non-interactive, visible in process listings)


.SH OPTIONS INHERITED FROM PARENT COMMANDS
\fB--color\fP="auto"
	When to emit ANSI color: auto, always, never

.PP
\fB--json\fP[=false]
	Output format shorthand for --output json; overrides --output when both are specified

.PP
\fB--no-pipe-warning\fP[=false]
	suppress 'reading from non-TTY' warning when piping secrets

.PP
\fB--output\fP="text"
	Output format (text, json, yaml)

.PP
\fB--profile\fP=""
	use a named vault profile

.PP
\fB--quiet\fP[=false]
	suppress non-error output

.PP
\fB--theme\fP=""
	Color preset: default, highcontrast, colorblind (or SYMVAULT_THEME)

.PP
\fB--vault\fP="~/.symvault"
	path to the password vault


.SH EXAMPLE
.EX
  symvault add github
  symvault add work/aws
  symvault add personal/bank
  symvault add github-token --value "my-secret-token"
  symvault add secure-pass --generate --length 20
  symvault add aws-key --type api_key --value "AKIA..."
  symvault add ssh-key --type ssh_key --usage-hint "Production server key"
.EE


.SH SEE ALSO
\fBsymvault(1)\fP

.SH NAME
symvault-agent-install - Install and configure an AI agent for Symaira Vault


.SH SYNOPSIS
\fBsymvault agent install [name] [flags]\fP


.SH DESCRIPTION
Unified install command that detects an AI agent, creates a security
profile in config.yaml, generates a scoped access token, injects the
MCP server configuration into the agent's config file, and installs the
embedded skill package — all in one step.

.PP
This replaces the older mcp install, mcp-config, and agent setup commands.

.PP
The default security tier is "safe" (read-only capabilities). For "standard"
or "admin" tiers, an interactive terminal is required to confirm the
security implications.

.PP
Supported agents: openclaw, claude-code, hermes, codex, opencode


.SH OPTIONS
\fB--auto-detect\fP[=false]
	Detect all installed agents and configure each

.PP
\fB--config-only\fP[=false]
	Only inject MCP config, skip the skill

.PP
\fB--dry-run\fP[=false]
	Preview changes without applying them

.PP
\fB--force\fP[=false]
	Overwrite existing agent profile and MCP config entries

.PP
\fB-h\fP, \fB--help\fP[=false]
	help for install

.PP
\fB--http\fP[=false]
	Use HTTP transport with auto-generated bearer token

.PP
\fB--skill-only\fP[=false]
	Only install the skill package, skip MCP config

.PP
\fB--tier\fP="safe"
	Security tier: safe (default), standard, or admin


.SH OPTIONS INHERITED FROM PARENT COMMANDS
\fB--color\fP="auto"
	When to emit ANSI color: auto, always, never

.PP
\fB--json\fP[=false]
	Output format shorthand for --output json; overrides --output when both are specified

.PP
\fB--no-pipe-warning\fP[=false]
	suppress 'reading from non-TTY' warning when piping secrets

.PP
\fB--output\fP="text"
	Output format (text, json, yaml)

.PP
\fB--profile\fP=""
	use a named vault profile

.PP
\fB--quiet\fP[=false]
	suppress non-error output

.PP
\fB--theme\fP=""
	Color preset: default, highcontrast, colorblind (or SYMVAULT_THEME)

.PP
\fB--vault\fP="~/.symvault"
	path to the password vault


.SH EXAMPLE
.EX
  # Install and configure Claude Code (auto-detect)
  symvault agent install claude-code

  # Detect all installed agents and configure each
  symvault agent install --auto-detect

  # HTTP transport with auto-generated bearer token
  symvault agent install hermes --http

  # Standard tier with explicit confirmation
  symvault agent install codex --tier standard

  # Preview what would happen without writing anything
  symvault agent install openclaw --dry-run

  # Only install the skill package, skip MCP config
  symvault agent install opencode --skill-only

  # Only inject MCP config, skip the skill
  symvault agent install claude-code --config-only

  # Force overwrite existing profile and MCP config entries
  symvault agent install hermes --force

  # Structured JSON output for scripting
  symvault agent install opencode --output json
.EE


.SH SEE ALSO
\fBsymvault-agent(1)\fP

.SH NAME
symvault-broker - Run the egress credential broker (loopback MITM proxy)


.SH SYNOPSIS
\fBsymvault broker [flags]\fP


.SH DESCRIPTION
Run an opt-in loopback MITM forward proxy that attaches vault
credentials to the agent's outbound HTTPS/HTTP requests server-side.

.PP
A brokered secret never enters the agent's process environment, argv or
process listing: the child process only receives HTTPS_PROXY/HTTP_PROXY and
the path to the broker's CA certificate. Hosts covered by an API template
get credential injection; unmatched hosts are forwarded untouched (or
rejected with 403 in --strict mode). Hosts in --passthrough are tunneled
without TLS interception (escape hatch for certificate-pinning clients).

.PP
Same-machine limitation: on one host this removes the plaintext from the
child environment, but an agent with the user's own filesystem access can
still reach the vault. Deploy the broker on a separate host (or the agent
in a container) for the strong guarantee.

.PP
The broker exits on SIGINT/SIGTERM. The generated CA certificate is written
to /broker-ca.pem.


.SH OPTIONS
\fB--addr\fP="127.0.0.1:0"
	Loopback listen address (0 selects an ephemeral port)

.PP
\fB-h\fP, \fB--help\fP[=false]
	help for broker

.PP
\fB--passthrough\fP=[]
	Hosts tunneled without TLS interception (comma-separated, domain suffixes match)

.PP
\fB--strict\fP[=false]
	Reject requests to hosts without a matching template with 403


.SH OPTIONS INHERITED FROM PARENT COMMANDS
\fB--color\fP="auto"
	When to emit ANSI color: auto, always, never

.PP
\fB--json\fP[=false]
	Output format shorthand for --output json; overrides --output when both are specified

.PP
\fB--no-pipe-warning\fP[=false]
	suppress 'reading from non-TTY' warning when piping secrets

.PP
\fB--output\fP="text"
	Output format (text, json, yaml)

.PP
\fB--profile\fP=""
	use a named vault profile

.PP
\fB--quiet\fP[=false]
	suppress non-error output

.PP
\fB--theme\fP=""
	Color preset: default, highcontrast, colorblind (or SYMVAULT_THEME)

.PP
\fB--vault\fP="~/.symvault"
	path to the password vault


.SH EXAMPLE
.EX
  # Start the broker on an ephemeral loopback port
  symvault broker

  # Fixed port, strict mode (unmatched hosts get 403)
  symvault broker --addr 127.0.0.1:8080 --strict

  # Pass through hosts whose clients pin certificates
  symvault broker --passthrough corporate.internal,legacy.example.com

  # Use with a child process (env exports are printed at startup)
  symvault run --broker -- gh pr create
.EE


.SH SEE ALSO
\fBsymvault(1)\fP

.SH NAME
symvault-device-join - Join an existing vault as a new device


.SH SYNOPSIS
\fBsymvault device join   [flags]\fP


.SH DESCRIPTION
Join an existing vault from a remote git repository.

.PP
Clones the vault repository, reads the pairing token file to obtain
the existing device's public key, generates a new identity for this device,
and submits this device's public key back to the vault.

.PP
After completion, the existing device must run 'symvault device accept \&'
to re-encrypt all entries for this new device.

.PP

--pairing-file. The file is the \&.json written by 'symvault device pair'
on the existing device; it can travel over any channel (synced folder, AirDrop,
manual copy). The response artifact is then left in the local vault directory
as -response.json for delivery back to the existing device by any
means; 'symvault device accept' accepts both -joined.json (git flow)
and -response.json (file flow).

.SH NAME

When --format is not specified, the format is auto-detected from the input file extension:

  .json → JSON format
  .yaml/.yml → YAML format
  .zip  → CXF format (FIDO Credential Exchange Format archive)

.PP
CSV files are additionally header-sniffed: exports from Apple Passwords
(iCloud Keychain), Chrome/Chromium and Firefox are recognized from their
header row and mapped with a built-in profile. Use --format apple, --format
chrome or --format firefox to select a profile explicitly. Use --format to
override auto-detection or when the file extension does not match the actual
format.

	Delete existing entries before writing

	Prepend path to all imported entries

	Import entries into quarantine// for human review before agent access

	Skip entries that already exist

	When to emit ANSI color: auto, always, never

.PP
\fB--json\fP[=false]
	Output format shorthand for --output json; overrides --output when both are specified

.PP
\fB--no-pipe-warning\fP[=false]
	suppress 'reading from non-TTY' warning when piping secrets

.PP
\fB--output\fP="text"
	Output format (text, json, yaml)

.PP
\fB--profile\fP=""
	use a named vault profile

.PP
\fB--quiet\fP[=false]
	suppress non-error output

.PP
\fB--theme\fP=""
	Color preset: default, highcontrast, colorblind (or SYMVAULT_THEME)

.PP
\fB--vault\fP="~/.symvault"
	path to the password vault


.SH EXAMPLE
.EX
  # Auto-detect format from file extension
  symvault import bw-export.json --dry-run

  # Auto-detect the CSV profile from the header row (Apple Passwords, Chrome, Firefox)

.SH NAME

.SH DESCRIPTION
Watches a user-selected folder for new credential material (screenshots,
exports, certificate files, backup codes) and stages each pickup as a
quarantined review batch under quarantine//. The watcher is
deliberately conservative:
.IP \(bu 2

partial downloads and files still being written are skipped.
.IP \(bu 2

and promotion happen through \fBimport review promote\fR\&.

file is not intaked twice.

always-on watcher, run without --once and stop it with Ctrl-C (SIGINT) or
SIGTERM; to pause, stop the process and restart it later. To disable, remove
the LaunchAgent entry or stop invoking the command.

.PP
Example LaunchAgent plist (adjust paths):
  ~/Library/LaunchAgents/com.symaira.vault-intake.plist
  ProgramArguments: [ /usr/local/bin/symvault, intake, watch, /path/to/folder, --once ]
  StartInterval: 300

.SH NAME

.SH SYNOPSIS
\fBsymvault migrate kdf [flags]\fP


.SH DESCRIPTION
Migrate the vault identity's key derivation function from the legacy
scrypt KDF to argon2id.

.PP
Argon2id is the industry standard for password hashing and provides stronger
resistance against GPU-based attacks than scrypt. New vaults already use
argon2id.

.PP
This command performs the migration itself — it does not just report status.
Automatic migration on every unlock additionally happens when
vault.auto_migrate_kdf: true is set in config.yaml, but by default that is
off, so this command is the way to upgrade an existing scrypt vault.

.PP
identity.age is backed up to identity.age.bak before any change, and the new
file is decrypt-verified before the migration is considered done. On any
failure the original identity.age is restored automatically. Changing
config.yaml's scrypt_work_factor alone does not perform this migration —
only this command (or auto_migrate_kdf) re-encrypts identity.age.

.PP

on their existing capabilities:
.IP \(bu 2

.IP \(bu 2

before any changes are written.

.PP
This migration is idempotent — running it multiple times is safe for
profiles that already have a tier field.


.SH OPTIONS

.SH NAME
symvault-run - Run a command with secrets injected as environment variables


.SH SYNOPSIS
\fBsymvault run [flags] --  [args...]\fP


.SH DESCRIPTION
Executes a command with vault secrets injected as environment variables. Use --env NAME=path.field to map secrets.

.PP
With --broker the child's outbound traffic is routed through an in-process egress credential broker, so brokered secrets never enter the child environment. The broker mode is configured with --broker-strict (reject hosts without a matching template) and --broker-passthrough (tunnel certificate-pinning hosts without TLS interception).


.SH OPTIONS
\fB--broker\fP[=false]
	Route the child's outbound traffic through the egress credential broker (credentials never enter the child environment); configure with --broker-strict and --broker-passthrough

.PP
\fB--broker-passthrough\fP=[]
	With --broker: hosts tunneled without TLS interception (comma-separated, domain suffixes match)

.PP
\fB--broker-strict\fP[=false]
	With --broker: reject requests to hosts without a matching template with 403

.PP
\fB-e\fP, \fB--env\fP=[]
	Environment variable mapping (NAME=path.field)

.PP
\fB-f\fP, \fB--env-file\fP=[]
	File with env variable mappings (NAME=path.field), one per line

.PP
\fB-h\fP, \fB--help\fP[=false]
	help for run

.PP
\fB--passthrough\fP=[]
	Parent env var names to pass through to the child process (comma-separated)

.PP
\fB-t\fP, \fB--timeout\fP=0s
	Timeout for the command (e.g., 30s)

.PP
\fB-C\fP, \fB--working-dir\fP=""
	Working directory for the command


.SH OPTIONS INHERITED FROM PARENT COMMANDS
\fB--color\fP="auto"
	When to emit ANSI color: auto, always, never

.PP
\fB--json\fP[=false]
	Output format shorthand for --output json; overrides --output when both are specified

.PP
\fB--no-pipe-warning\fP[=false]
	suppress 'reading from non-TTY' warning when piping secrets

.PP
\fB--output\fP="text"
	Output format (text, json, yaml)

.PP
\fB--profile\fP=""
	use a named vault profile

.PP
\fB--quiet\fP[=false]
	suppress non-error output

.PP
\fB--theme\fP=""
	Color preset: default, highcontrast, colorblind (or SYMVAULT_THEME)

.PP
\fB--vault\fP="~/.symvault"
	path to the password vault


.SH EXAMPLE
.EX
  # Inject AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY from vault entry "work/aws.secret"
  symvault run --env AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY=work/aws.secret -- aws s3 ls

  # Multiple secrets from env file
  symvault run --env-file .env.symvault -- npm run dev

  # Pass through parent NODE_ENV and PORT to the child process
  NODE_ENV=production PORT=8080 symvault run --passthrough NODE_ENV,PORT -- npm start

  # Route the child through the egress broker: strict mode, with one
  # certificate-pinning host tunneled without TLS interception
  symvault run --broker --broker-strict --broker-passthrough corp.internal -- ./deploy.sh

  # Multiple secrets, custom working dir
  symvault run \\
    --env DB_PASS=prod/db.password \\
    --env API_TOKEN=stripe.token \\
    --workdir /tmp/job -- ./deploy.sh
.EE

\fBsymvault(1)\fP

.SH NAME
symvault-agent-install - Install and configure an AI agent for Symaira Vault


.SH SYNOPSIS
\fBsymvault agent install [name] [flags]\fP


.SH DESCRIPTION
Unified install command that detects an AI agent, creates a security
profile in config.yaml, generates a scoped access token, injects the
MCP server configuration into the agent's config file, and installs the
embedded skill package — all in one step.

.PP
This replaces the older mcp install, mcp-config, and agent setup commands.

.PP
The default security tier is "safe" (read-only capabilities). For "standard"
or "admin" tiers, an interactive terminal is required to confirm the
security implications.

.PP
Supported agents: openclaw, claude-code, hermes, codex, opencode


.SH OPTIONS
\fB--auto-detect\fP[=false]
	Detect all installed agents and configure each

.PP
\fB--config-only\fP[=false]
	Only inject MCP config, skip the skill

.PP
\fB--dry-run\fP[=false]
	Preview changes without applying them

.PP
\fB--force\fP[=false]
	Overwrite existing agent profile and MCP config entries

.PP
\fB-h\fP, \fB--help\fP[=false]
	help for install

.PP
\fB--http\fP[=false]
	Use HTTP transport with auto-generated bearer token

.PP
\fB--skill-only\fP[=false]
	Only install the skill package, skip MCP config

.PP
\fB--tier\fP="safe"
	Security tier: safe (default), standard, or admin


.SH OPTIONS INHERITED FROM PARENT COMMANDS
\fB--color\fP="auto"
	When to emit ANSI color: auto, always, never

.PP
\fB--json\fP[=false]
	Output format shorthand for --output json; overrides --output when both are specified

.PP
\fB--no-pipe-warning\fP[=false]
	suppress 'reading from non-TTY' warning when piping secrets

.PP
\fB--output\fP="text"
	Output format (text, json, yaml)

.PP
\fB--profile\fP=""
	use a named vault profile

.PP
\fB--quiet\fP[=false]
	suppress non-error output

.PP
\fB--theme\fP=""
	Color preset: default, highcontrast, colorblind (or SYMVAULT_THEME)

.PP
\fB--vault\fP="~/.symvault"
	path to the password vault


.SH EXAMPLE
.EX
  # Install and configure Claude Code (auto-detect)
  symvault agent install claude-code

  # Detect all installed agents and configure each
  symvault agent install --auto-detect

  # HTTP transport with auto-generated bearer token
  symvault agent install hermes --http

  # Standard tier with explicit confirmation
  symvault agent install codex --tier standard

  # Preview what would happen without writing anything
  symvault agent install openclaw --dry-run

  # Only install the skill package, skip MCP config
  symvault agent install opencode --skill-only

  # Only inject MCP config, skip the skill
  symvault agent install claude-code --config-only

  # Force overwrite existing profile and MCP config entries
  symvault agent install hermes --force

  # Structured JSON output for scripting
  symvault agent install opencode --output json
.EE


.SH SEE ALSO
\fBsymvault-agent(1)\fP

agent's profile in config.yaml. Use --yes to skip the confirmation prompt.

.SH NAME
symvault-broker - Run the egress credential broker (loopback MITM proxy)


.SH SYNOPSIS
\fBsymvault broker [flags]\fP


.SH DESCRIPTION
Run an opt-in loopback MITM forward proxy that attaches vault
credentials to the agent's outbound HTTPS/HTTP requests server-side.

.PP
A brokered secret never enters the agent's process environment, argv or
process listing: the child process only receives HTTPS_PROXY/HTTP_PROXY and
the path to the broker's CA certificate. Hosts covered by an API template
get credential injection; unmatched hosts are forwarded untouched (or
rejected with 403 in --strict mode). Hosts in --passthrough are tunneled
without TLS interception (escape hatch for certificate-pinning clients).

.PP
Same-machine limitation: on one host this removes the plaintext from the
child environment, but an agent with the user's own filesystem access can
still reach the vault. Deploy the broker on a separate host (or the agent
in a container) for the strong guarantee.

.PP
The broker exits on SIGINT/SIGTERM. The generated CA certificate is written
to /broker-ca.pem.


.SH OPTIONS
\fB--addr\fP="127.0.0.1:0"
	Loopback listen address (0 selects an ephemeral port)

.PP
\fB-h\fP, \fB--help\fP[=false]
	help for broker

.PP
\fB--passthrough\fP=[]
	Hosts tunneled without TLS interception (comma-separated, domain suffixes match)

.PP
\fB--strict\fP[=false]
	Reject requests to hosts without a matching template with 403

	suppress non-error output

	Color preset: default, highcontrast, colorblind (or SYMVAULT_THEME)

	path to the password vault

.PP
Clones the vault repository, reads the pairing token file to obtain
the existing device's public key, generates a new identity for this device,
and submits this device's public key back to the vault.

.PP

to re-encrypt all entries for this new device.

.PP

--pairing-file. The file is the \&.json written by 'symvault device pair'
on the existing device; it can travel over any channel (synced folder, AirDrop,
manual copy). The response artifact is then left in the local vault directory
as -response.json for delivery back to the existing device by any
means; 'symvault device accept' accepts both -joined.json (git flow)
and -response.json (file flow).

.SH NAME
symvault-intake-watch - Watch a folder for new credential files and stage quarantined batches


.SH SYNOPSIS
\fBsymvault intake watch  [flags]\fP


.SH DESCRIPTION
Watches a user-selected folder for new credential material (screenshots,
exports, certificate files, backup codes) and stages each pickup as a
quarantined review batch under quarantine//. The watcher is
deliberately conservative:
.IP \(bu 2
Files are only picked up after their size and mtime stabilized (debounce);
partial downloads and files still being written are skipped.
.IP \(bu 2
Sources are never deleted, never moved, and never auto-promoted. Review
and promotion happen through \fBimport review promote\fR\&.
.IP \(bu 2
Already-staged files are remembered across polls (ledger), so the same
file is not intaked twice.

.PP
Run with --once for a single scan (cron/LaunchAgent friendly). For an
always-on watcher, run without --once and stop it with Ctrl-C (SIGINT) or
SIGTERM; to pause, stop the process and restart it later. To disable, remove
the LaunchAgent entry or stop invoking the command.

.PP
Example LaunchAgent plist (adjust paths):
  ~/Library/LaunchAgents/com.symaira.vault-intake.plist
  ProgramArguments: [ /usr/local/bin/symvault, intake, watch, /path/to/folder, --once ]
  StartInterval: 300


.SH OPTIONS
\fB--debounce\fP=5s
	Require files to be stable for this long before pickup

.PP
\fB-h\fP, \fB--help\fP[=false]
	help for watch

.PP
\fB--interval\fP=10s
	Poll interval (always-on mode)

.PP

	Emit machine-readable JSON per scan

.PP

	Run a single scan and exit

.SH NAME
symvault-intake - Review-gated credential intake from loose files


.SH SYNOPSIS
\fBsymvault intake  [flags]\fP


.SH DESCRIPTION
Validates loose credential material (text files, .env exports, JSON,
screenshots, certificate/key files, backup-code images) and stages it as a
quarantined review batch under quarantine// for human review
before any agent can read it.

.PP
Sources are validated (regular files only, stable size/mtime, per-file and
batch limits), copied atomically into a private spool, content-sniffed (never
trusting extensions), and parsed into field/attachment suggestions. The
exact source bytes are stored as an encrypted attachment with SHA-256, size
and source-type provenance. Nothing is written to normal vault paths.

.PP
Promote a batch after review:
  symvault intake review promote    (alias of import review promote)

.PP
Source files are never deleted unless --move-to-trash is given (macOS only)
and only after the quarantine entry was written and verified.

\fB--batch-limit\fP=33554432
	Maximum total bytes per intake run

.PP
\fB--dry-run\fP[=false]
	Validate and report without writing anything

	Maximum number of files per intake run

.SH NAME
symvault-migrate-kdf - Migrate the vault identity from scrypt to argon2id


.SH SYNOPSIS
\fBsymvault migrate kdf [flags]\fP


.SH DESCRIPTION
Migrate the vault identity's key derivation function from the legacy
scrypt KDF to argon2id.

.PP
Argon2id is the industry standard for password hashing and provides stronger
resistance against GPU-based attacks than scrypt. New vaults already use
argon2id.

.PP
This command performs the migration itself — it does not just report status.
Automatic migration on every unlock additionally happens when
vault.auto_migrate_kdf: true is set in config.yaml, but by default that is
off, so this command is the way to upgrade an existing scrypt vault.

.PP
identity.age is backed up to identity.age.bak before any change, and the new
file is decrypt-verified before the migration is considered done. On any
failure the original identity.age is restored automatically. Changing
config.yaml's scrypt_work_factor alone does not perform this migration —
only this command (or auto_migrate_kdf) re-encrypts identity.age.

.SH NAME

.SH DESCRIPTION

	suppress non-error output

.PP

.SH NAME
symvault-run - Run a command with secrets injected as environment variables


.SH SYNOPSIS
\fBsymvault run [flags] --  [args...]\fP


.SH DESCRIPTION
Executes a command with vault secrets injected as environment variables. Use --env NAME=path.field to map secrets.

.PP
With --broker the child's outbound traffic is routed through an in-process egress credential broker, so brokered secrets never enter the child environment. The broker mode is configured with --broker-strict (reject hosts without a matching template) and --broker-passthrough (tunnel certificate-pinning hosts without TLS interception).


.SH OPTIONS
\fB--broker\fP[=false]
	Route the child's outbound traffic through the egress credential broker (credentials never enter the child environment); configure with --broker-strict and --broker-passthrough

.PP
\fB--broker-passthrough\fP=[]
	With --broker: hosts tunneled without TLS interception (comma-separated, domain suffixes match)

.PP
\fB--broker-strict\fP[=false]
	With --broker: reject requests to hosts without a matching template with 403

.PP
\fB-e\fP, \fB--env\fP=[]
	Environment variable mapping (NAME=path.field)

.PP
\fB-f\fP, \fB--env-file\fP=[]
	File with env variable mappings (NAME=path.field), one per line

.PP
\fB-h\fP, \fB--help\fP[=false]
	help for run

.PP
\fB--passthrough\fP=[]
	Parent env var names to pass through to the child process (comma-separated)

.PP
\fB-t\fP, \fB--timeout\fP=0s
	Timeout for the command (e.g., 30s)

.PP
\fB-C\fP, \fB--working-dir\fP=""
	Working directory for the command


.SH OPTIONS INHERITED FROM PARENT COMMANDS
\fB--color\fP="auto"
	When to emit ANSI color: auto, always, never

.PP
\fB--json\fP[=false]

.PP

.PP

.SH NAME
symvault-broker - Run the egress credential broker (loopback MITM proxy)


.SH SYNOPSIS
\fBsymvault broker [flags]\fP


.SH DESCRIPTION
Run an opt-in loopback MITM forward proxy that attaches vault
credentials to the agent's outbound HTTPS/HTTP requests server-side.

.PP
A brokered secret never enters the agent's process environment, argv or
process listing: the child process only receives HTTPS_PROXY/HTTP_PROXY and
the path to the broker's CA certificate. Hosts covered by an API template
get credential injection; unmatched hosts are forwarded untouched (or
rejected with 403 in --strict mode). Hosts in --passthrough are tunneled
without TLS interception (escape hatch for certificate-pinning clients).

.PP
Same-machine limitation: on one host this removes the plaintext from the
child environment, but an agent with the user's own filesystem access can
still reach the vault. Deploy the broker on a separate host (or the agent
in a container) for the strong guarantee.

.PP
The broker exits on SIGINT/SIGTERM. The generated CA certificate is written
to /broker-ca.pem.


.SH OPTIONS
\fB--addr\fP="127.0.0.1:0"
	Loopback listen address (0 selects an ephemeral port)

.PP
\fB-h\fP, \fB--help\fP[=false]
	help for broker

.PP
\fB--passthrough\fP=[]
	Hosts tunneled without TLS interception (comma-separated, domain suffixes match)

.PP
\fB--strict\fP[=false]
	Reject requests to hosts without a matching template with 403


.SH OPTIONS INHERITED FROM PARENT COMMANDS
\fB--color\fP="auto"
	When to emit ANSI color: auto, always, never

.PP
\fB--json\fP[=false]
	Output format shorthand for --output json; overrides --output when both are specified

.PP
\fB--no-pipe-warning\fP[=false]
	suppress 'reading from non-TTY' warning when piping secrets

.PP
\fB--output\fP="text"
	Output format (text, json, yaml)

.PP
\fB--profile\fP=""
	use a named vault profile

.PP
\fB--quiet\fP[=false]
	suppress non-error output

.PP
\fB--theme\fP=""
	Color preset: default, highcontrast, colorblind (or SYMVAULT_THEME)

.PP
\fB--vault\fP="~/.symvault"
	path to the password vault


.SH EXAMPLE
.EX
  # Start the broker on an ephemeral loopback port
  symvault broker

  # Fixed port, strict mode (unmatched hosts get 403)
  symvault broker --addr 127.0.0.1:8080 --strict

  # Pass through hosts whose clients pin certificates
  symvault broker --passthrough corporate.internal,legacy.example.com

  # Use with a child process (env exports are printed at startup)
  symvault run --broker -- gh pr create
.EE

.SH NAME
symvault-device-join - Join an existing vault as a new device


.SH SYNOPSIS
\fBsymvault device join   [flags]\fP


.SH DESCRIPTION
Join an existing vault from a remote git repository.

.PP
Clones the vault repository, reads the pairing token file to obtain
the existing device's public key, generates a new identity for this device,
and submits this device's public key back to the vault.

.PP
After completion, the existing device must run 'symvault device accept \&'
to re-encrypt all entries for this new device.

.PP
To join without a git remote, pass the invitation artifact directly with
--pairing-file. The file is the \&.json written by 'symvault device pair'
on the existing device; it can travel over any channel (synced folder, AirDrop,
manual copy). The response artifact is then left in the local vault directory
as -response.json for delivery back to the existing device by any
means; 'symvault device accept' accepts both -joined.json (git flow)
and -response.json (file flow).

.SH NAME
symvault-doctor - Check vault health and configuration


.SH SYNOPSIS
\fBsymvault doctor [flags]\fP


.SH DESCRIPTION
Run a series of health checks on the current vault and report their status.

.PP
Output modes:
  --text (default): colored output, one line per check
  --json:           machine-readable JSON (suitable for CI/monitoring)

.PP
Use --no-network to skip checks that require network access (git remote reachability, update check).


.SH OPTIONS
\fB--exclude\fP=[]
	Skip checks matching these glob patterns (comma-separated)

.PP
\fB--fix\fP[=false]
	auto-repair safe issues (permissions, gitignore, git init)

.PP
\fB--fix-dry-run\fP[=false]
	Log what --fix would do without modifying anything

.PP
\fB-h\fP, \fB--help\fP[=false]
	help for doctor

.PP
\fB--json\fP[=false]
	Output in JSON format (deprecated: use --output=json)

.PP
\fB--no-network\fP[=false]
	Skip network-dependent checks

.PP
\fB--only\fP=[]
	Only run checks matching these glob patterns (comma-separated, e.g. vault.*)

.PP
\fB--quick\fP[=false]
	Skip slow checks (scrypt benchmark, update check)

.PP
\fB--strict\fP[=false]
	Return non-zero exit code for warnings (7) or failures (8)


.SH OPTIONS INHERITED FROM PARENT COMMANDS
\fB--color\fP="auto"
	When to emit ANSI color: auto, always, never

.PP
\fB--no-pipe-warning\fP[=false]
	suppress 'reading from non-TTY' warning when piping secrets

.PP
\fB--output\fP="text"
	Output format (text, json, yaml)

.PP
\fB--profile\fP=""
	use a named vault profile

.PP
\fB--quiet\fP[=false]
	suppress non-error output

.PP
\fB--theme\fP=""
	Color preset: default, highcontrast, colorblind (or SYMVAULT_THEME)

.PP
\fB--vault\fP="~/.symvault"
	path to the password vault


.SH EXAMPLE
.EX
  # Full health check
  symvault doctor

  # JSON output, no network
  symvault doctor --output json --no-network

  # Run only config checks
  symvault doctor --only 'config.*'

  # Auto-fix what's safe to fix (with dry-run first)
  symvault doctor --fix-dry-run
  symvault doctor --fix
.EE

\fBsymvault(1)\fP

.SH NAME
symvault-intake-watch - Watch a folder for new credential files and stage quarantined batches


.SH SYNOPSIS
\fBsymvault intake watch  [flags]\fP


.SH DESCRIPTION
Watches a user-selected folder for new credential material (screenshots,
exports, certificate files, backup codes) and stages each pickup as a
quarantined review batch under quarantine//. The watcher is
deliberately conservative:
.IP \(bu 2
Files are only picked up after their size and mtime stabilized (debounce);
partial downloads and files still being written are skipped.
.IP \(bu 2
Sources are never deleted, never moved, and never auto-promoted. Review
and promotion happen through \fBimport review promote\fR\&.
.IP \(bu 2
Already-staged files are remembered across polls (ledger), so the same
file is not intaked twice.

.PP
Run with --once for a single scan (cron/LaunchAgent friendly). For an
always-on watcher, run without --once and stop it with Ctrl-C (SIGINT) or
SIGTERM; to pause, stop the process and restart it later. To disable, remove
the LaunchAgent entry or stop invoking the command.

.PP
Example LaunchAgent plist (adjust paths):
  ~/Library/LaunchAgents/com.symaira.vault-intake.plist
  ProgramArguments: [ /usr/local/bin/symvault, intake, watch, /path/to/folder, --once ]
  StartInterval: 300


.SH OPTIONS
\fB--debounce\fP=5s
	Require files to be stable for this long before pickup

.PP
\fB-h\fP, \fB--help\fP[=false]
	help for watch

.PP
\fB--interval\fP=10s
	Poll interval (always-on mode)

.PP
\fB--json\fP[=false]
	Emit machine-readable JSON per scan

.PP
\fB--once\fP[=false]
	Run a single scan and exit


.SH OPTIONS INHERITED FROM PARENT COMMANDS
\fB--color\fP="auto"
	When to emit ANSI color: auto, always, never

.PP
\fB--no-pipe-warning\fP[=false]
	suppress 'reading from non-TTY' warning when piping secrets

.PP
\fB--output\fP="text"
	Output format (text, json, yaml)

.PP
\fB--profile\fP=""
	use a named vault profile

.PP
\fB--quiet\fP[=false]
	suppress non-error output

.PP
\fB--theme\fP=""
	Color preset: default, highcontrast, colorblind (or SYMVAULT_THEME)

.PP
\fB--vault\fP="~/.symvault"
	path to the password vault


.SH EXAMPLE
.EX
  # One scan, stage anything new (cron-friendly)
  symvault intake watch ~/Downloads/intake --once

  # Machine-readable single scan
  symvault intake watch ~/Downloads/intake --once --json

  # Always-on watcher with a 15s poll interval

.SH NAME
symvault-intake - Review-gated credential intake from loose files


.SH SYNOPSIS
\fBsymvault intake  [flags]\fP


.SH DESCRIPTION
Validates loose credential material (text files, .env exports, JSON,
screenshots, certificate/key files, backup-code images) and stages it as a
quarantined review batch under quarantine// for human review
before any agent can read it.

.PP
Sources are validated (regular files only, stable size/mtime, per-file and
batch limits), copied atomically into a private spool, content-sniffed (never
trusting extensions), and parsed into field/attachment suggestions. The
exact source bytes are stored as an encrypted attachment with SHA-256, size
and source-type provenance. Nothing is written to normal vault paths.

.PP
Promote a batch after review:
  symvault intake review promote    (alias of import review promote)

.PP
Source files are never deleted unless --move-to-trash is given (macOS only)
and only after the quarantine entry was written and verified.


.SH OPTIONS
\fB--batch-limit\fP=33554432
	Maximum total bytes per intake run

.PP
\fB--dry-run\fP[=false]
	Validate and report without writing anything

.PP
\fB-h\fP, \fB--help\fP[=false]
	help for intake

.PP
\fB--json\fP[=false]
	Emit machine-readable JSON (metadata only, never secret values)

.PP
\fB--max-files\fP=100
	Maximum number of files per intake run

.PP
\fB--move-to-trash\fP[=false]
	Move verified source files to the macOS Trash after the quarantine entry is written (macOS only)

.PP

	suppress 'reading from non-TTY' warning when piping secrets

\fB--output\fP="text"
	Output format (text, json, yaml)

	use a named vault profile

.SH EXAMPLE

.SH NAME
symvault-migrate-kdf - Migrate the vault identity from scrypt to argon2id


.SH SYNOPSIS
\fBsymvault migrate kdf [flags]\fP


.SH DESCRIPTION
Migrate the vault identity's key derivation function from the legacy
scrypt KDF to argon2id.

.PP
Argon2id is the industry standard for password hashing and provides stronger
resistance against GPU-based attacks than scrypt. New vaults already use
argon2id.

.PP
This command performs the migration itself — it does not just report status.
Automatic migration on every unlock additionally happens when
vault.auto_migrate_kdf: true is set in config.yaml, but by default that is
off, so this command is the way to upgrade an existing scrypt vault.

.PP
identity.age is backed up to identity.age.bak before any change, and the new
file is decrypt-verified before the migration is considered done. On any
failure the original identity.age is restored automatically. Changing
config.yaml's scrypt_work_factor alone does not perform this migration —
only this command (or auto_migrate_kdf) re-encrypts identity.age.

.SH NAME
symvault-run - Run a command with secrets injected as environment variables


.SH SYNOPSIS
\fBsymvault run [flags] --  [args...]\fP


.SH DESCRIPTION
Executes a command with vault secrets injected as environment variables. Use --env NAME=path.field to map secrets.

.PP
With --broker the child's outbound traffic is routed through an in-process egress credential broker, so brokered secrets never enter the child environment. The broker mode is configured with --broker-strict (reject hosts without a matching template) and --broker-passthrough (tunnel certificate-pinning hosts without TLS interception).


.SH OPTIONS
\fB--broker\fP[=false]
	Route the child's outbound traffic through the egress credential broker (credentials never enter the child environment); configure with --broker-strict and --broker-passthrough

.PP
\fB--broker-passthrough\fP=[]
	With --broker: hosts tunneled without TLS interception (comma-separated, domain suffixes match)

.PP
\fB--broker-strict\fP[=false]
	With --broker: reject requests to hosts without a matching template with 403

.PP
\fB-e\fP, \fB--env\fP=[]
	Environment variable mapping (NAME=path.field)

.PP
\fB-f\fP, \fB--env-file\fP=[]
	File with env variable mappings (NAME=path.field), one per line

.PP
\fB-h\fP, \fB--help\fP[=false]
	help for run

.PP
\fB--passthrough\fP=[]
	Parent env var names to pass through to the child process (comma-separated)

.PP
\fB-t\fP, \fB--timeout\fP=0s
	Timeout for the command (e.g., 30s)

.PP
\fB-C\fP, \fB--working-dir\fP=""
	Working directory for the command


.SH OPTIONS INHERITED FROM PARENT COMMANDS
\fB--color\fP="auto"
	When to emit ANSI color: auto, always, never

.PP
\fB--json\fP[=false]
	Output format shorthand for --output json; overrides --output when both are specified

.PP
\fB--no-pipe-warning\fP[=false]
	suppress 'reading from non-TTY' warning when piping secrets

.PP
\fB--output\fP="text"
	Output format (text, json, yaml)

.PP
\fB--profile\fP=""
	use a named vault profile

.PP
\fB--quiet\fP[=false]
	suppress non-error output

.PP
\fB--theme\fP=""
	Color preset: default, highcontrast, colorblind (or SYMVAULT_THEME)

.PP
\fB--vault\fP="~/.symvault"
	path to the password vault


.SH EXAMPLE
.EX
  # Inject AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY from vault entry "work/aws.secret"
  symvault run --env AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY=work/aws.secret -- aws s3 ls

  # Multiple secrets from env file
  symvault run --env-file .env.symvault -- npm run dev

  # Pass through parent NODE_ENV and PORT to the child process
  NODE_ENV=production PORT=8080 symvault run --passthrough NODE_ENV,PORT -- npm start

  # Route the child through the egress broker: strict mode, with one
  # certificate-pinning host tunneled without TLS interception
  symvault run --broker --broker-strict --broker-passthrough corp.internal -- ./deploy.sh

  # Multiple secrets, custom working dir
  symvault run \\
    --env DB_PASS=prod/db.password \\
    --env API_TOKEN=stripe.token \\
    --workdir /tmp/job -- ./deploy.sh
.EE


.SH SEE ALSO
\fBsymvault(1)\fP

.SH NAME
symvault-template-generate - Generate a configuration file from a template


.SH SYNOPSIS
\fBsymvault template generate [KEY=ref ...] [flags]\fP


.SH DESCRIPTION
Generate a configuration file from a template.

.PP
Refs can be specified as positional KEY=ref arguments or via --prefix to
automatically select entries matching a vault path prefix. Each ref is a
vault entry path with an optional dot-separated field (e.g. db.password).
When --prefix is used without positional args, all matching entries are
included with the entry basename as the key.


.SH OPTIONS
\fB--dry-run\fP[=false]
	Show template with masked values

.PP
\fB-h\fP, \fB--help\fP[=false]
	help for generate

.PP
\fB--name\fP="app"
	Name of the resource being generated

.PP
\fB--output\fP=""
	Output file path (optional)

.PP
\fB--prefix\fP=""
	Vault path prefix to auto-select entries (e.g. work/)

.PP
\fB--type\fP=""
	Template type (env, docker-compose, k8s-secret, github-actions, terraform)


.SH OPTIONS INHERITED FROM PARENT COMMANDS
\fB--color\fP="auto"
	When to emit ANSI color: auto, always, never

.PP
\fB--json\fP[=false]
	Output format shorthand for --output json; overrides --output when both are specified

.PP
\fB--no-pipe-warning\fP[=false]
	suppress 'reading from non-TTY' warning when piping secrets

.PP
\fB--profile\fP=""
	use a named vault profile

.PP
\fB--quiet\fP[=false]
	suppress non-error output

.PP
\fB--theme\fP=""
	Color preset: default, highcontrast, colorblind (or SYMVAULT_THEME)

.PP
\fB--vault\fP="~/.symvault"
	path to the password vault


.SH EXAMPLE
.EX
  # Generate .env file from specific vault secrets
  symvault template generate --type env DB_PASS=prod/db.password API_KEY=stripe.token

  # Generate .env from all entries under work/
  symvault template generate --type env --prefix work/

  # Generate Kubernetes secret manifest with mixed refs
  symvault template generate --type k8s-secret --name prod-secrets --prefix work/ DB_HOST=infra.db.host

  # Dry-run to preview without real values
  symvault template generate --type env --prefix work/ --dry-run
.EE


.SH SEE ALSO
\fBsymvault-template(1)\fP

.SH NAME
symvault-unlock - Unlock the vault and cache the passphrase


.SH SYNOPSIS
\fBsymvault unlock [flags]\fP


.SH DESCRIPTION
Unlock the vault by validating the passphrase and caching it in the
OS keyring. This allows MCP servers to start without interactive prompts.

.PP
Use --check to verify if an active session exists without prompting.

.PP
Environment variable SYMVAULT_PASSPHRASE
can be used for non-interactive unlock in CI/CD environments, but only when
explicitly allowed via SYMVAULT_ALLOW_ENV_PASSPHRASE=1 or
security.allow_env_passphrase: true in config.yaml — the passphrase variable
alone is ignored (default-deny). It should NOT be used on shared machines
(visible in process listings).

.SH NAME
symvault-verify - Verify vault entry integrity against manifest


.SH SYNOPSIS
\fBsymvault verify [flags]\fP


.SH DESCRIPTION
Verify that all vault entries match their recorded manifest hashes.
This detects tampered or corrupted entry files.

.PP
Use --rebuild to regenerate the manifest from the on-disk .age files (use
this when entries have been added out-of-band, e.g. via git sync, and the
manifest has not been updated). Use --rebuild-only to skip the integrity
check and only rebuild.


.SH OPTIONS
\fB-h\fP, \fB--help\fP[=false]
	help for verify

.PP
\fB--rebuild\fP[=false]
	Rebuild the manifest from on-disk entries after the integrity check

.PP
\fB--rebuild-only\fP[=false]
	Rebuild the manifest and skip the integrity check


.SH OPTIONS INHERITED FROM PARENT COMMANDS
\fB--color\fP="auto"
	When to emit ANSI color: auto, always, never

.PP
\fB--json\fP[=false]
	Output format shorthand for --output json; overrides --output when both are specified

.PP
\fB--no-pipe-warning\fP[=false]
	suppress 'reading from non-TTY' warning when piping secrets

.PP
\fB--output\fP="text"
	Output format (text, json, yaml)

.PP
\fB--profile\fP=""
	use a named vault profile

.PP
\fB--quiet\fP[=false]
	suppress non-error output

.PP
\fB--theme\fP=""
	Color preset: default, highcontrast, colorblind (or SYMVAULT_THEME)

.PP
\fB--vault\fP="~/.symvault"
	path to the password vault


.SH EXAMPLE
.EX
  # Verify manifest matches on-disk entries
  symvault verify

  # Rebuild the manifest from on-disk entries (fixes "unknown" entries from sync)
  symvault verify --rebuild

  # Just rebuild, skip the integrity check
  symvault verify --rebuild-only

  # As part of a scripted health check
  symvault verify || echo "Manifest mismatch — investigate"
.EE


.SH SEE ALSO

.SH NAME
symvault - Symaira Vault is a Go CLI password manager


.SH SYNOPSIS
\fBsymvault [flags]\fP


.SH DESCRIPTION
Quick Start:
  symvault init            create a vault and identity
  symvault add       add a credential
  symvault get       retrieve a credential

.PP
Symaira Vault is a Go CLI password manager with an interactive TUI, multi-device
sync via Git, and an MCP server for AI-agent integration.

.PP
First-time setup:
   1. symvault init         create a vault and identity (non-interactive)
   2. symvault setup        same, plus guided wizard for sync/agents (TTY only)
   3. symvault doctor       health-check and self-heal

.PP
Daily use:
  symvault add       add a credential (interactive form)
  symvault ui              browse and edit the vault in a TUI
  symvault get       print a credential
  symvault --help          full command list


.SH OPTIONS
\fB--color\fP="auto"
	When to emit ANSI color: auto, always, never

.PP
\fB-h\fP, \fB--help\fP[=false]
	help for symvault

.PP
\fB--json\fP[=false]
	Output format shorthand for --output json; overrides --output when both are specified

.PP
\fB--no-pipe-warning\fP[=false]
	suppress 'reading from non-TTY' warning when piping secrets

.PP
\fB--output\fP="text"
	Output format (text, json, yaml)

.PP
\fB--profile\fP=""
	use a named vault profile

.PP
\fB--quiet\fP[=false]
	suppress non-error output

.PP
\fB--theme\fP=""
	Color preset: default, highcontrast, colorblind (or SYMVAULT_THEME)

.PP
\fB--vault\fP="~/.symvault"
	path to the password vault
